pr.title: Create an `AllocId` for `ConstValue::Slice`.
pr.description:
This PR modifies `ConstValue::Slice` to use an `AllocId` instead of directly manipulating the allocation. This was originally proposed by https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/115764 but was a perf regression.

Almost 2 years later, enough code has changed to make this a perf improvement: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/116707#issuecomment-3067158777
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: This PR (rust-lang/rust#116707) is a missed-optimization change, not a correctness fix. It changes ConstValue::Slice to store a deduplicated AllocId, so repeated identical slice literals now share an allocation and GVN can fold direct pointer-equality of two equal literals from a runtime Eq (old behavior: false, because each use could get a fresh allocation) to const true. The pre-change conservative behavior was legal: Rust gives no guarantee that equal string/slice literals have equal addresses. Consequently there is no historical "incorrect transformation" to witness. On the fixed modern compiler, equal const slice bytes already deduplicate, so the old conservative result (distinct addresses) cannot be reproduced from a faithful source-level ConstValue::Slice scenario. Any attempt to force two equal-byte literals to have different addresses would require unrelated constructs (separate statics, stack locals, heap buffers) and would not encode this PR's transformation. The indirect identity-call path also remains semantically consistent because the opaque calls still return the same deduplicated pointer value. Hence no valid source-grounded differing pair can be validated under the fixed compiler and Miri.

analysis.summary: Changing `ConstValue::Slice` from an inline `ConstAllocation` to an `AllocId` makes identical string/byte-slice literals deduplicate to the same allocation. As a result, slice constants become deterministic, and GVN can propagate them and fold direct equality of two equal literals (`Eq` -> `const true`). Values obtained through separate non-inlined calls must still not be assumed equal.
analysis.originalLogic: `ConstValue::Slice` stored `data: ConstAllocation<'tcx>` plus `meta`, and consumers such as codegen/interpreter called `reserve_and_set_memory_alloc(data)` to manufacture an `AllocId` per use. `Const::is_deterministic` therefore had a special case: `Const::Val(ConstValue::Slice { .. }, _) => false`, with the comment "If the same slice appears twice in the MIR, we cannot guarantee that we will give the same `AllocId` to the data." GVN consequently did not treat slice constants as deterministic/propagatable, and the old `duplicate_slice` MIR expectation kept the direct equality as a runtime `Eq` with the comment "`direct` must not fold to `true`, as `indirect` will not."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-change transformation under test is the conservative one: GVN leaves two directly compared, byte-identical slice literals as runtime `Eq(copy _1, copy _2)` and keeps the second literal as an allocation/copy rather than a reusable constant (old expected `_2 = copy _8 as u128` and `_9 = Eq(copy _1, copy _2)`). This was not a miscompile; it was a missed optimization caused by fresh per-use allocations. After the PR, `ConstValue::Slice { alloc_id, meta }` is deduplicated through `allocate_bytes_dedup`, `Const::is_deterministic` returns true for slices, and GVN emits `_1 = const "a" as u128`, `_2 = copy _1`, `_9 = const true`, `_0 = (const true, copy _10)`. The indirect case `_10 = Eq(copy _3, copy _4)` remains because those operands come from separate calls and are not proven equal.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR constants of slice/reference types (`&str`, `&[u8]`, CStr) whose value is `ConstValue::Slice`, especially repeated identical literal bytes within one function, and comparisons/transmutes of their pointer halves. The relevant invariant is that immutable const bytes allocated with the same salt and same contents receive the same `AllocId`. Source programs with two direct equal literals versus the same literals passed through separate opaque/identity calls exercise the boundary of what GVN may fold.
analysis.trigger: Two MIR operands are `ConstValue::Slice` constants with identical bytes and the same dedup salt, so they share an `AllocId`; slice constants are now deterministic, allowing GVN constant propagation and folding of direct pointer/integer equality. Equality of results returned by distinct non-inlined calls remains runtime, even if the underlying literal is the same.
preconditions: The slice points to immutable const data, so sharing one `AllocId` is sound.
Identical bytes are allocated through the same dedup salt (e.g. `CTFE_ALLOC_SALT`) so the `AllocId` is actually reused.
GVN sees a supported constant operand (not an unsized local) and the comparison is between the direct constant-derived values.
Indirect values produced by separate calls are not assumed equal merely because their literal argument bytes are equal.
pitfalls: Do not expect `identity(const "a") == identity(const "a")` to fold just because the argument literal is deduplicated; the two call results are distinct SSA values in the test and the equality must remain.

The many added `ALLOC0`/`ALLOC1`/... dumps in mir-opt expectations for other passes are mostly because slice allocations are now printed/collected, not evidence that those passes changed their transformation semantics.

Do not infer a stable source-level guarantee that equal string literals have equal addresses; this PR makes dedup an implementation fact that enables the optimization, and the old conservative behavior was legal.

When converting `Slice` to an `AllocId`, all consumers that used to hold the allocation inline must keep/collect that allocation; the monomorphize collector now collects the slice's own `AllocId`, and codegen no longer calls `reserve_and_set_memory_alloc`.
The diagnostics helper changed offset/length handling from an end offset to `start + len`; tests should not conflate that refactor with the GVN equality change.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the MIR-opt GVN tests `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` (`slices` and `duplicate_slice`) with `-Zdump-mir=GVN`. For `duplicate_slice`, check the direct path becomes `_1 = const "a" as u128`, `_2 = copy _1`, `_9 = const true`, and `_0 = (const true, copy _10)`, while `_10 = Eq(copy _3, copy _4)` (via two `identity` calls) is still not folded. For `slices`, check repeated uses are again represented as `const` rather than only copies. Add a control program where the two compared operands are results of separate non-inlined calls to ensure GVN does not over-fold. The Miri test `src/tools/miri/tests/pass/const-addrs.rs` should assert one deduplicated base address per const: "Check that we always return the same base address for the const allocation." and `assert_eq!(addrs.len(), 1);`. No compiler build or execution was performed for this knowledge entry; these are source- and MIR-diff-based expectations.
